newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 37 trln lire BOTs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 37 trln lire BOTs.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is set to issue 36 to 38 trillion lire ($22.6 billion) of short-term BOT bills at its auction on February 25, with the average issuance seen at 37 trillion lire against 39.81 trillion lire of bills expiring, analysts said.

For zero-coupon CTZ paper, there is 10.056 trillion lire expiring. Analysts see 2.5 trillion lire of 18-month paper being issued at the Feb 25 auction with a range of 2 to 3 trillion and 3 trillion of 24-month CTZs with a range of 2.5 to 5.0 trillion.

All analysts expect the Treasury to issue fewer BOTs than those expiring. But for CTZs, the average forecast is for a slightly greater total issue of new paper than is expiring. Analysts noted that the Treasury has already issued 4.7 trillion lire of CTZs at its middle of the month auction earlier in February.
The settlement date for the BOTs and CTZs is February 28, while the actual quantities will be announced after the bond market has closed on February 20.
